content:
Evan R. (Finance): quick thread 
We need a final reconciliation vendor rec. Finalists: ReconWorks, LedgerLoop, and ParseGrid. Execs want a 1-page with recommended vendor + 3 negotiation anchors by Friday EOD. Can procurement lead?
Maya S. (Procurement): I'll take point. What must the 1-pager include? My checklist: 12mo TCO, pilot terms, commit minimums, migration credits, SLA credits, and top legal risks.
Jonas M. (EngOps): add integration effort (eng-weeks), supported ingest types (Snowflake/S3/Kafka), reprocess policy (are historical re-runs billable?), and webhook concurrency. Also note any native connectors.
Kiera (ReconWorks Sales): ReconWorks has native Snowflake and Kafka ingest, offers a 45-day pilot with up to $6k credit, and supports customer-managed keys. Reprocesses during pilot are free; prod reprocesses are negotiable.
vendor-bot: "ReconWorks: SOC2 Type II available; sample 500-invoice anonymized set available after NDA"
Priya V. (Legal): include DPA, subprocessor list, indemnity cap, data return timing, and a clause requiring parser-accuracy SLA with credits for regressions. If any vendor forces a hard minimum commit without strong PS credits, flag it.
Evan R. (Finance): Ops fallback cost: assume $X per 1k invoices processed manually (please compute). Also include retention/archival cost assumptions (30/90/180 days).
Maya S. (Procurement): I'll request rate cards with line-item breakouts: list price, commit tiers, overage rates, export/egress fees, long-term retention cost, and professional services rates.
Jonas M. (EngOps): quick tech notes from demos: LedgerLoop needs a custom DB connector (no native Snowflake), ParseGrid has the cleanest schema mapping UI but charges per-schema change after onboarding. That will affect ops costs.
Kiera (ReconWorks Sales): for negotiation, ReconWorks can waive schema-change fees for the first 6 months and include 120-day retention in enterprise deals. We can also agree to a pilot-to-contract credit applied against first invoice if you sign within 30 days.
Priya V. (Legal): ask vendors for sample contract language for data deletion and a certification of deletion on termination. Also request any carveouts around aggregated analytics they keep.
Maya S. (Procurement): action items: 1) I'll collect pricing and push for pilot credits + migration credits. 2) Jonas to estimate eng-weeks for each vendor. 3) Priya to draft redlines for indemnity and commit escape clauses. 4) Evan will model TCO with sensitivity (20% up/down).
Jonas M. (EngOps): preliminary engineering estimates: ReconWorks = 3 engineer-days (Snowflake + mapping), LedgerLoop = 2 engineer-weeks (custom connector), ParseGrid = 1 engineer-week + 2 days for mapping validation. I'll confirm with teams and post numbers.
Evan R. (Finance): good. For scoring weights I'm proposing Cost 50%, Integration 20%, Features 20%, Legal/Risk 10% for this exec ask. Any objections?
Priya V. (Legal): fine. One legal ask: insist on an SLA credit mechanism tied to parser accuracy (e.g., <95% accuracy on our test set = 10% monthly credit). Push for an indemnity cap meaningful relative to our exposure.
Maya S. (Procurement): noted. I'll ask vendors to confirm whether they can meet an accuracy SLA and what credits they'd offer. If a vendor refuses to commit to accuracy credits, that's a negative.
Kiera (ReconWorks Sales): ReconWorks willing to sign accuracy credits on our enterprise plan; we'll provide baseline accuracy report on a 500-sample test if NDA ok.
Evan R. (Finance): timeline: procurement posts rate cards by Thu noon; eng posts integration deltas Thu 3pm; legal posts redlines Thu 5pm. I'll assemble the 1-pager Thu evening and circulate for quick review before Friday exec snapshot.
Maya S. (Procurement): quick FYI: LedgerLoop previously offered a 10% pilot credit but also requested a 6mo commit; I'll push to convert that into PS credits instead of hard spend.
Jonas M. (EngOps): another note: check retention default -- LedgerLoop's default is 30 days, which will bump archival costs if we need longer. Include that in TCO.
Priya V. (Legal): will prepare redline template and escalate any vendor with aggressive indemnity or data-use clauses. Also request subprocessor SOC2 for all vendors.
Evan R. (Finance): perfect. If we can get a guaranteed pilot accuracy report and firm pilot credits, that will heavily influence recommendation. Thanks team 44d
Maya S. (Procurement): will update here as responses come in. If vendors push minimums, procurement will request PS or migration credits instead.
